content: 1. If the dose of isoniazid (INH) exceeds 10 mg/kg/day, it is recommended to supplement with 50–100 mg of pyridoxine daily. Isoniazid reduces pyridoxine levels through an unspecified interaction mechanism. 2. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of rabeprazole by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 3. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of ramelteon by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 4. Isoniazid decreases the effects of repaglinide through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 5. Isoniazid decreases the effects of rosiglitazone through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 6. Isoniazid decreases the effects of sitagliptin through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 7. Triamcinolone acetonide injectable suspension reduces the effects of isoniazid through an unknown mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 8. Isoniazid increases the levels of valproic acid by reducing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 9. Isoniazid decreases the effects of vildagliptin through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 10. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of zaleplon by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 11. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of ziprasidone by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 12. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of zolpidem by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 13. Both 5-HTP and isoniazid increase serotonin levels. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 14. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of abemaciclib by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increase plasma levels of abemaciclib and its metabolites, necessitating dose reduction. If the strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is discontinued, the abemaciclib dose should be increased to the pre-inhibition level. 15. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of abrocitinib by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. When co-administered with CYP2C19 inhibitors, abrocitinib should be initiated at 50 mg daily. If an adequate response is not achieved after 12 weeks, the dose may be increased to 100 mg daily. Discontinue treatment if no adequate response is observed after the dosage increase. 16. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of acalabrutinib by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A inhibitors should be avoided. If short-term use of a strong CYP3A inhibitor (e.g., up to 7 days) is necessary, temporarily interrupt acalabrutinib treatment. 17. Isoniazid decreases the effects of acarbose through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 18. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of acetaminophen by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2E1 metabolism. It also increases acetaminophen toxicity through an unknown mechanism. Close monitoring is recommended. 19. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of ado-trastuzumab emtansine by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase exposure to DM1, the cytotoxic component, leading to increased toxicity. Alternative therapy is recommended. 20. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of alfentanil by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, and alternative therapy is recommended. Monitor for excessive central nervous system and respiratory depression. 21. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of alosetron by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 22. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of alprazolam by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 23. Aluminum hydroxide reduces isoniazid levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by at least 2 hours. 24. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of ambrisentan by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 25. Isoniazid increases the toxicity of amifampridine. Amifampridine can cause seizures, and co-administration with drugs that lower the seizure threshold may increase this risk. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 26. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of amiodarone by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 27. Isoniazid increases serotonin levels when co-administered with amitriptyline. It also increases the levels or effects of amitriptyline by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is recommended. 28. Isoniazid increases serotonin levels when co-administered with amoxapine. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 29. Isoniazid increases serotonin levels when co-administered with amphetamine. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 30. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of apalutamide by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Dose reduction may be necessary based on tolerability. 31. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of aprepitant by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 32. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of aripiprazole by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 33. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of armodafinil by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 34. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of artemether/lumefantrine by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 35. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of atazanavir by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 36. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of atogepant by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. The recommended atogepant dosage is 10 mg orally once daily when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 37. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of atorvastatin by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 38. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of avanafil by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated due to the risk of severe adverse events, including hypotension, syncope, visual changes, and priapism. 39. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of avapritinib by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors should be avoided. If unavoidable, reduce the starting dose of avapritinib. 40. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of axitinib by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors should be avoided. If unavoidable, reduce the axitinib dose by 50%. 41. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 42. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of bedaquiline by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors for more than 14 consecutive days should be avoided unless the benefits outweigh the risks. 43. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of belzutifan by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Monitor for anemia and hypoxia, and adjust the belzutifan dose as recommended. 44. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of benzhydrocodone/acetaminophen by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase hydrocodone plasma concentrations, potentially leading to fatal respiratory depression. 45. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of bexarotene by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 46. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of bortezomib by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 47. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of bosentan by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 48. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of bosutinib by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors should be avoided. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increase bosutinib plasma concentrations approximately fivefold. 49. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of brentuximab vedotin by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and patients should be monitored for adverse reactions. 50. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of brexpiprazole by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Adjust the brexpiprazole dose based on the presence of CYP2D6 and CYP3A4 inhibitors. 51. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of brigatinib by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A inhibitors should be avoided. If unavoidable, reduce the brigatinib dose by approximately 50%. 52. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of budesonide by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Budesonide may reduce the effects of isoniazid through an unknown mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 53. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of buprenorphine subdermal implant by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. If necessary, consider implant removal and transition to a buprenorphine dosage form that allows dose adjustments. 54. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of buprenorphine long-acting injection by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Transition patients back to a buprenorphine formulation that permits dose adjustments if toxicity or overdose occurs. 55. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of buspirone by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Both buspirone and isoniazid increase serotonin levels. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 56. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of cabazitaxel by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors should be avoided. 57. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of cabozantinib by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors should be avoided. If unavoidable, reduce the cabozantinib dose and resume the previous dose 2–3 days after discontinuation of the strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. 58. Isoniazid affects the metabolism of calcifediol by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 activity. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. CYP450 inhibitors may interfere with enzymes involved in vitamin D metabolism (CYP24A1 and CYP27B1).
